issues.body: The note corrects a stale count by writing a new literal count into markdown. No test pins the size of the recognised set: there is no assertion on DTYPE_TABLE.len() or on Recognized::standard() cardinality anywhere in crates/sparq-reason/src/dtype.rs or crates/sparq-reason/tests/, so the next time a datatype is enrolled in DTYPE_TABLE this document silently becomes wrong again in exactly the way it is being fixed for now. This is mildly in tension with the note's own premise that DTYPE_TABLE is the single source of truth: the durable statement is 'derived from DTYPE_TABLE', while '30' is a snapshot that has to be hand-maintained. Not blocking — the number is accurate today, the file is explicitly a historical design record rather than live API documentation, and the banner already tells readers not to treat the surrounding inventory as current.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) drop the specific figure and say 'Recognized::standard() is now table-driven from DTYPE_TABLE and has been broadened beyond this list; consult DTYPE_TABLE for the current membership', which cannot go stale; or (b) keep '30' and add a cheap guard in crates/sparq-reason/src/dtype.rs tests, e.g. assert_eq!(DTYPE_TABLE.len(), 30) with a comment pointing at research/d-entailment-datatype-map.md, so enrolling a new datatype forces the doc update in the same change.
issues.title: Fix trades one unpinned hard-coded count (23) for another (30) with no test guarding drift

verdict.summary: Documentation-only change: adds a historical-snapshot banner to research/d-entailment-datatype-map.md warning that the 23-datatype inventory recorded below is the PRE-broadening state, and that Recognized::standard() is now table-driven with 30 datatypes. No code, test, or build surface is touched, so there is no correctness, soundness, or security impact. I verified every factual claim in the added note against the head checkout: (1) 'table-driven' is accurate — Recognized::standard() (crates/sparq-reason/src/dtype.rs:223) is derived by filtering DTYPE_TABLE (line 141) on the has_value_mapping flag, and the module doc (lines 70-79) documents that table as the single source of truth for both the recognised set and has_value_mapping, introduced by sq-pbz04.6.2. (2) The count of 30 is correct — DTYPE_TABLE holds 7 string-family entries (string, normalizedString, token, language, Name, NCName, NMTOKEN), boolean, 13 integer types, decimal/double/float, dateTime/dateTimeStamp/date, anyURI, and hexBinary/base64Binary = 30, all with has_map = true, so the filter admits all of them. The counting convention matches the original '23 datatypes' bullet (XSD table entries only; rdf:langString, added by Recognized::default(), is out of the XSD namespace and was excluded from the old count too), so 23 -> 30 is an apples-to-apples correction. (3) 'After D2' resolves correctly — bead D2 in the same record's section 5 table is precisely the map-broadening plus single-table refactor that added anyURI, the token-derived string types, and the binary types. The banner also does not overreach: the doc is already labelled a DESIGN + DECOMPOSITION RECORD, and the facet-soundness gaps listed further down in section 1 remain correctly framed as design-time findings tracked by bead D1, so the historical framing is consistent with the rest of the file.
